body.heading: Saying it without sending it
paragraphs: There are letters that would help to write and harm to send: to someone who has died, someone who would not understand, or a past version of yourself. Writing the unsent letter lets you say the complete, unedited thing — gratitude, anger, apology, all of it.
Because nobody will read it, you do not have to be fair, brief or reasonable. You only have to be accurate about what you feel, which is harder and more useful than it sounds.

body.heading: What to do with it afterwards
paragraphs: Keep it, seal it, or destroy it — all are legitimate endings, and destroying it can be its own small ceremony. Some people write one every year to the same person, and reading the series shows how much has shifted.
If writing brings up feelings that stay heavy for a long time, that is worth sharing with a trusted person or a counsellor. The letter is a beginning, not a replacement for support.

takeaway: Write it fully, send it never — some letters are for the writer.
